responses:
The parent already implements directed SPH multistart; attempt 1's ordering tweak produced identical cost (627.1164), so diversifying terminal orderings alone has no leverage here. I'll instead refine the SPH mechanism itself with a **terminal-cascade attachment**: when SPH attaches a terminal via its winning path, that path may pass through other *unplaced* terminals. Currently those are left in the queue and re-attached in later Dijkstra sweeps (at zero marginal cost, but the extra sweeps change which terminal is "cheapest" next and can yield worse arborescences). Marking every terminal lying on the winning path as immediately placed (a) reduces sweeps, and (b) structurally changes the tree: subsequent attachments are forced to branch off a richer partial tree, which often shares more trunk edges. This is a genuine refinement of the working mechanism, strictly bounded (it can only *reduce* the number of Dijkstra sweeps per start), and the best-of-seeds commit keeps it monotone.
